findings.title: consecutive_progressing_cycles semantics — counts windows not distinct boredom events
findings.resolution: No code change. Semantics confirmed: consecutive_progressing_cycles counts consecutive 1h windows from newest where new_shapes_introduced > 0. Current value = 4 (all four windows progressing). The S.4a lift criterion used this field but required 3 across 4h windows. With 4 windows and all progressing, the criterion is currently met. However, the semantic ambiguity remains — the field is a window-count, not a distinct boredom-fire-count as the S.4a spec implied. LOW severity maintained. Operator should note this interpretation difference.

evidence.calculation: for i in [0..3]: if cells_over_time[i].new_shapes_introduced > 0: consecutive_progressing_cycles++; else break
evidence.semantics_note: Counts consecutive non-empty windows from newest end. Not monotonic across polling calls. A window can be empty in the next poll if no executions happen in that hour.

findings.title: Spec inconsistency: tasks.md 1.1 regex requires 3-part event types; design/implementation accept 2-part
findings.description: openspec tasks.md §1.1 specifies the event type regex as ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ (exactly 3 parts). The design.md, spec files, and implementation all use 2-part names: vessel.registered, vessel.heartbeat, vessel.expired, vessel.deregistered. The implementation regex is /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*){1,3}$/ (2-4 parts), which correctly accepts the vessel.* events. The tasks.md regex would reject the very events tasks 4.1-4.4 require. The implementation is correct; the tasks.md has a documentation error in its proposed regex.

evidence.verdict: Implementation is correct; tasks.md §1.1 has a documentation-level error (would reject the events it requires in §4)
